```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B identifies a concrete payer (the platform, not the end user) and backs a price hypothesis with sourced competitor price lists: not.bot at $9.99–$249/mo and useHUMA up to $499/mo. Businesses are at least being offered paid tiers. A's own brief says 'No clean single payer found', and every named competitor is free to the user, funded by grants, VC or nonprofit dues.",
    "For a paying customer within 90 days, B has a sourced low-cost self-serve channel: a Product Hunt-style developer launch at roughly $200–$500. A's paid channel is consumer app-install ads at $1–$5 CPI, driving users to a product nobody in the category charges for. A's other channel, advocacy nonprofits, already run their own free tools, and the brief shows no evidence they would buy.",
    "A's plausible payers (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants) rest only on a grant-funded analog and are not tied to any purchase evidence. They also imply slow procurement or grant cycles, so none of A's payer paths shows a realistic sale inside 90 days.",
    "B's risks are real but scoped in the brief. Bank and enterprise sales take 6–18 months and require SOC 2, so they are out of reach. Free tiers compress pricing, and biometric rules (BIPA/GDPR) apply. A non-biometric, self-serve niche such as small marketplaces, dating apps or review sites stays reachable, and B's sourced competitor price lists give it a payment path that A's evidence lacks."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's central monetization claim in 'Case For', that there is 'a credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants)', has no source and counts as missing. The only cited example of non-consumer funding is a $930,000 public-health research grant to BikeMaps.org. That is grant funding, not a customer purchase, and nothing in the brief shows a city or advocacy group paying a third-party vendor for this.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B wins mainly because A has no evidenced payer at all. B's own evidence has gaps. Its demand evidence is anecdotal: a Reddit quote, an executive's promotional statement, and a single deepfake fraud incident. Its pricing comes from competitor list prices, with no data on conversion or whether small platforms actually buy from a new solo vendor. Four free-tier competitors and biometric-privacy exposure could push B toward zero revenue in the reachable segment. B also references an 'open_questions' field that is not included in the brief."
}
```
